title: Crestline Refunds Posted to the Crestline Credit Card as Merchandise Credits
content:
A Crestline refund on a ticket that was paid with the Crestline Credit Card posts to the card as a merchandise credit for the refund amount. It posts also on a suspended or closed account.

## Which balance the credit reduces

The credit reduces the balance of the original ticket:

- when that ticket is on a promotional plan, the credit reduces the plan's remaining balance and is not available to pay other balances;
- when the credit exceeds what remains on the plan, the excess reduces the standard balance.

## What a merchandise credit is not

A merchandise credit is never a payment: it does not count toward the minimum payment due and does not stop a late fee for a missed minimum.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Original ticket | Remaining on its plan | Credit | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| on a 12-month deferred plan | 500 USD | 200 USD | the plan's remaining balance falls to 300 USD |
| on a 12-month deferred plan | 120 USD | 200 USD | the plan falls to 0; the other 80 USD reduces the standard balance |
| a standard purchase | — | 75 USD | reduces the standard balance |

A cardholder whose statement minimum is 40 USD and who receives a 150 USD merchandise credit before the due date, but makes no payment, has still not paid the minimum.
